As a proto-gamer who grew up with the NES, I completely agree with Kimmel; and so does every other gamer I know.

Watching people play video games is OKAY in small, non-frequent bursts. Watching people play video games as your primary hobby (and I do believe that is what Kimmel was specifically talking about) is total crap and I'd almost consider it a form of mental illness.

All of the outrage, as far as I can see, is coming from young millenials that aren't even real gamers in the first place.

You would seriously consider it a mental illness, akin to depression or schizophrenia? Like Draco said, it's just a hobby. I don't really understand what's fun about watching someone else play a video game either, but thinking of it as a mental illness is a bit of an overreaction.
I agree with Kimmell. Watching other people play video games when you could be playing them yourself is retarded. I guess I'm getting old.
Watching other people play sports when you could be playing them yourself is retarded.

The difference is, it is very easy to get a multiplayer game started. Most have matchmaking of some sort, so you're in and playing within ~15 minutes of deciding to play.

With sports, you have to have the proper equipment (same with games, so rule this one out), the proper playing field (the back yard works) and the most important part, other players. So, if I wanted to get a game of basketball going, the equipment and playing field are easy, but the travel time and getting together other players makes this a much longer activity.

With video games, I can be doing nearly anything at home and be playing a game with other people within minutes of deciding to play. Then be done playing and do something else if need be in a short amount of time.

Whereas with sports, it can take 15 minutes to an hour just to get people together at a playing field. Then, once done you still have the travel time back home and a likely shower afterwards. This turns it into a multi-hour long activity.

All that said, in my opinion, watching other people play video games you own is stupid, unless it is a competitive game (LoL, CS:GO). That makes sense as you're watching not just for entertainment, but also to learn.
